name: Zep
note: Temporal knowledge-graph memory service (Graphiti).

name: MemOS
note: Memory operating system from MemTensor.

name: memU
note: Open-source memory framework.

name: LangMem
note: LangChain's long-term memory SDK.

name: MemTree
note: Tree-structured dynamic memory; re-run by H-Mem.

name: Think-in-Memory (TiM)
note: Stores inductive thoughts instead of raw turns.

name: OpenAI memory
note: ChatGPT's built-in memory feature, used as a baseline.

name: RAG (chunked)
note: Retrieval over fixed-size chunks; variant names the chunk size and k.

name: Nemori
note: Self-organizing memory inspired by cognitive science.

name: Recursive summary
note: MemGPT's baseline: the LLM reads a lossy summary of past sessions.

name: Native compaction
note: OpenAI Responses API context compaction, used by SelfMem.

name: LoCoMo-style memory
note: The observation/summary memory baseline from the LoCoMo paper.

name: Memobase
note: User-profile memory backend.

name: MemoRAG
note: Memory-inspired RAG (WWW 2025).

name: Human reference
note: Human-written gold output; a reference point, not a system.

name: Engram
note: Baseline in True Memory; the paper gives no citation.

name: BM25
note: Plain lexical retrieval baseline.

name: Supermemory
note: Hosted memory API.

name: No memory
note: The answering model with no conversation history.

name: Letta
note: MemGPT's successor framework.

name: Session-level RAG
note: Retrieves whole sessions; SeCom baseline.

name: Conversation Summary Memory
note: LangChain summary memory; SeCom baseline.

name: GraphRAG
note: LLM-extracted knowledge graph split into communities (Leiden) with LLM community summaries.

name: Gemini 1.5 Pro
note: Proprietary MLLM (video baseline in EventMemAgent).

name: GPT-4o
note: Proprietary MLLM (video baseline in EventMemAgent).

name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
note: Proprietary MLLM (video baseline in EventMemAgent).

name: Qwen2-VL
note: Open-source offline video MLLM; 7B and 72B rows.

name: Qwen3-VL
note: Open-source offline MLLM; the 8B model is EventMemAgent's backbone.

name: LLaVA-Video
note: Open-source offline video MLLM (7B); EventMemAgent cites Video-LLaVA for this row.

name: LLaVA-OneVision
note: Open-source offline MLLM (7B).

name: InternVL-V2
note: Open-source offline MLLM (8B); cited to Science China Information Sciences 2024.

name: LongVU
note: Offline long-video MLLM with spatiotemporal token compression (7B).

name: Flash-VStream
note: Online video MLLM with a compressed visual memory (7B); EventMemAgent also cites the 2025 version, arXiv 2506.23825.

name: VideoLLM-online
note: Online streaming video LLM (8B), CVPR 2024.

name: Dispider
note: Online video MLLM with disentangled perception, decision and reaction (7B), CVPR 2025.

name: StreamForest
note: Online video MLLM with persistent event memory (7B).

name: StreamAgent
note: Prompted online video agent (7B).

name: TimeChat-Online
note: Online video MLLM that drops redundant visual tokens (7B), ACM MM 2025.

name: VideoLLaMA 2
note: Open-source offline video MLLM (7B).

name: VILA-1.5
note: Open-source offline MLLM (8B); EventMemAgent cites NVILA (CVPR 2025) for this row.

name: Video-CCAM
note: Open-source offline video MLLM (14B).

name: LongVA
note: Long-context offline video MLLM (7B).

name: Kangaroo
note: Long-context offline video MLLM (7B).

name: LLaVA-NeXT-Video
note: Offline video MLLM (32B row).

name: MiniCPM-V 2.6
note: Open-source offline MLLM (8B).

name: MEM1
note: RL-trained agent that keeps one compact internal state paragraph while it reads and retrieves.

name: LD-Agent
note: Hello Again! LLM-powered personalized agent for long-term dialogue (NAACL 2025; arXiv 2406.05925): long/short-term memory banks with keyword-based retrieval.

name: G-Memory
note: G-Memory: Tracing Hierarchical Memory for Multi-Agent Systems; SEDM describes it as hierarchical tracing over a global pool searched by similarity.

name: WebShaper
note: Information-seeking web agent trained on formalization-driven synthesized data (32B model).

name: LangChain Open Deep Research
note: Open-source deep-research agent from LangChain.

name: Doubao Deep Research
note: Proprietary deep-research product (ByteDance).

name: Kimi Deep Research
note: Proprietary deep-research product (Moonshot AI).

name: Claude Research
note: Proprietary deep-research feature of Claude (Anthropic).

name: OpenAI Deep Research
note: Proprietary deep-research agent (OpenAI).

name: Gemini 2.5 Pro Deep Research
note: Proprietary deep-research agent (Google).

name: MOOM
note: Memory system for ultra-long role-play dialogues, from the authors of the ZH-4O benchmark.

name: FIFO truncation
note: Keeps only the most recent k interaction turns and drops older ones; variant names k.

name: Turn retrieval
note: Keeps the k past interaction turns most similar (by embedding) to the latest turn, plus the latest turn; ACON baseline.

name: LLMLingua
note: Extractive prompt compression with a small LM that drops low-information tokens (LLMLingua-2: arXiv 2403.12968); variant names keep rate.

name: Prompted LLM compression
note: An LLM summarizes the agent's history or observation with a general hand-written instruction; ACON's naive-prompting baseline.

name: FT (constrained fine-tuning)
note: Fine-tuning with a norm constraint (Zhu et al. 2020), as run in AlphaEdit; distinct from WISE's FT-L runs.

name: InstructEdit
note: MEND-style meta-learned editor trained with task instructions.

name: PRUNE
note: Restrains the condition number of the edited matrix during sequential editing (reimplemented by AlphaEdit).

name: RECT
note: Regularises MEMIT-style weight updates to protect general abilities.

name: SERAC
note: Memory-based editor: stores edits explicitly, a scope classifier routes in-scope inputs to a counterfactual model.

name: MELO
note: Neuron-indexed dynamic LoRA blocks activated per edit.

name: SteP
note: Stacked LLM policies for web actions, with human-written per-website policies.

name: WebArena baseline agent
note: The prompted LLM agent reported with the WebArena benchmark.

name: AutoEval
note: Autonomous evaluation and refinement of digital agents with a model-based evaluator.

name: BrowserGym agent
note: Generic prompted web agent in the BrowserGym environment (here with GPT-4o).

name: VisualWebArena baseline agent
note: The prompted multimodal agent reported with the VisualWebArena benchmark.

name: Tree Search (Koh et al.)
note: Best-first tree search over web actions with an LLM value function.

name: Self-RAG
note: LM trained to decide when to retrieve and to critique retrieved passages with reflection tokens.

name: IRCoT
note: Interleaves chain-of-thought steps with retrieval, using each new thought as the next query; variant names the index it runs on.

name: ReAct
note: Prompted agent loop that alternates reasoning, action and observation, appending the full history.

name: CodeAct
note: Agent that writes its actions as executable Python code.

name: Plan-and-Solve
note: Prompting that writes a plan first and then executes it step by step.

name: AgentLM
note: Llama-2 instruction-tuned on agent trajectories (AgentTuning).

name: WebThinker
note: Reasoning model that interleaves thinking with web search and page exploration.

name: HiRA
note: Hierarchical deep-search agent: planner, coordinator and specialised executors with dual-channel memory.

name: DFSDT
note: Depth-first search decision tree for tool use, from ToolLLM.

name: EasyTool
note: Rewrites tool documentation once into concise tool instructions with an LLM.

name: InfLLM
note: Training-free KV-cache memory: past tokens in fixed-size blocks, each with representative tokens, retrieved by k-NN into the context window (Xiao et al., NeurIPS 2024). EM-LLM builds on its code.

name: Nest
note: Semi-parametric, retrieval-based decoding (nearest-neighbour speculative decoding); EWE runs it with 100 retrieved candidate passages.

name: DRAGIN
note: Iterative RAG that pauses when a confidence score mixing attention and entropy drops and builds a keyword query from attended tokens.

name: Chain-of-Verification (CoVe)
note: Prompting method in which the LLM verifies and revises its own draft without retrieval; EWE uses the factor+revise variant.

name: Act
note: ReAct without the reasoning (thought) steps; actions only.

name: Imitation learning (BUTLER / WebShop IL)
note: Trained imitation-learning agents whose numbers ExpeL copies from the ReAct paper (BUTLER on ALFWorld, the WebShop IL model).

name: Least-to-Most (agent adaptation)
note: Decompose into subquestions (subgoals) and solve them in order; HiAgent's 'w. TD' baseline keeps the full history.

name: Tree-Planner
note: Closed-loop LLM task planner that samples plans into an action tree; compared by HiAgent on Tyreworld.

name: GPT-4.1
note: OpenAI LLM, direct-inference baseline without tools (IterResearch Table 1).

name: o4-mini
note: OpenAI reasoning model, direct-inference baseline.

name: DeepSeek-R1
note: Reasoning LLM; variant names the checkpoint (e.g. 0528).

name: Perplexity Deep Research
note: Proprietary deep-research product (Perplexity).

name: Grok 3 Research (DeepSearch)
note: Proprietary deep-research mode of Grok 3 (xAI).

name: Search-o1
note: Agentic search-enhanced large reasoning model; variant names the backbone.

name: WebDancer
note: Autonomous information-seeking web agent.

name: ASearcher
note: Long-horizon agentic search trained with large-scale asynchronous RL.

name: WebSailor
note: Web agent trained for super-human-level information seeking; variant names model size.

name: MiroThinker
note: Open-source deep-research agent from MiroMind; variant names size and version.

name: Fine-tuning (edit baseline)
note: Gradient steps on the one fact to change, all layers or a chosen layer; knowledge-editing baseline.

name: Constrained fine-tuning (Zhu et al. 2020)
note: Modifying Memories in Transformer Models: fine-tuning with a norm constraint between original and edited parameters.

name: Transformer (no memory)
note: Plain segment-by-segment Transformer with no memory across segments; baseline in Memoria.

name: Transformer-XL
note: Segment-level recurrence: caches the previous segment's hidden states as extra keys and values.

name: Compressive Transformer
note: Transformer-XL plus a compressed memory of older activations.

name: ∞-former
note: Long-term memory as a continuous-space attention over past hidden states.

name: BERT
note: Pre-trained encoder (bert-base-uncased in Memoria), 512-token input.

name: RoBERTa
note: Pre-trained encoder (base), 512-token input.

name: BigBird
note: Sparse-attention encoder, 4,096-token input.

name: Longformer
note: Sliding-window plus global attention encoder, 4,096-token input.

name: GPT-2
note: Pre-trained decoder (small, large, XL) fine-tuned without memory; baseline in Memoria Table 8.

name: Search-R1
note: LLM trained with RL to interleave reasoning and search calls, ReAct-style history.

name: AutoRefine
note: RL-trained search agent that refines retrieved evidence during thinking.

name: ReSearch
note: RL-trained model that reasons with search, keeping the full interaction history.

name: ZeroSearch
note: RL training of search agents with a simulated search engine.

name: O2-Searcher
note: Search-based agent for open-domain open-ended QA.

name: R1-Searcher
note: Two-stage RL training that incentivises search during reasoning.

name: Standard (no strategy planning)
note: Dialogue agent LLM prompted to reply without any explicit strategy; the base row in PRINCIPLES Table 1.

name: Proactive
note: Deng et al. 2023: prompt the LLM to pick the next strategy from a pre-defined set before replying.

name: ProCoT
note: Deng et al. 2023: chain-of-thought analysis of the dialogue, then a pre-defined strategy.

name: PPDPP
note: Plug-and-play policy planner (Deng et al. 2024): small LM planner trained by SFT on labelled strategies and RL from self-play AI feedback.

name: Ask-an-Expert (AnE)
note: Zhang et al. 2023: an LLM acting as expert infers the user's state and writes an open-ended strategy.

name: ICL-AIF
note: Fu et al. 2023: open-ended strategy suggestions from iterative AI feedback in self-play.

name: DPDP
note: He et al. 2024: dual-process dialogue planning with MCTS-based strategy selection.

name: GPT-4
note: The LLM used directly, one sample per problem, no memory or retries (code baseline in Reflexion).

name: CodeT
note: Code generation that scores sampled programs with model-generated tests; no memory.

name: Chain-of-Thought
note: Step-by-step prompting without tools or memory; in Reflexion's CoT (GT) variant the gold context is given.

name: OpenClaw (vanilla)
note: Open agent harness used as the unmanaged baseline in TokenPilot: built-in compaction only (500k window, trigger ratio 0.5).

name: LLMLingua-2
note: Token-level prompt compression with a small model (Findings of ACL 2024); TokenPilot used compression ratio 0.6.

name: Selective Context
note: Self-information-based pruning of low-information text (EMNLP 2023); TokenPilot used ratio 0.4.

name: LCM (Lossless Context Management)
note: Hierarchical-summary compaction with retained recent turns (Voltropy technical report, 2026).

name: Pichay
note: Demand paging for LLM context windows: utility-driven eviction of old tool results.

name: Summary (hierarchical compaction)
note: Generic baseline in TokenPilot: history compressed into hierarchical summaries at 40% of a 500k window.

name: MemoBrain
note: Executive memory for agent reasoning with a memory budget and recall.

name: AgentSwing
note: Adaptive context-management routing (discard-all, keep-last-n, summary) for long-horizon web agents.

name: Keep-Last-N
note: Generic baseline: keep only the most recent N turns once context passes a threshold (N = 5 in TokenPilot).

name: FT-L
note: Fine-tuning one MLP layer with a norm constraint, in ROME's reimplementation (WISE adds a KL term).

name: FT-EWC
note: Fine-tuning with Elastic Weight Consolidation, as reimplemented in GRACE.

name: MEND
note: Hypernetwork that turns fine-tuning gradients into low-rank weight edits.

name: ROME
note: Locate-then-edit: rank-one update to one mid-layer MLP found by causal tracing.

name: MEMIT
note: Locate-then-edit over several MLP layers with a least-squares update; MEMIT-MASS is its batch mode.

name: DEFER
note: GRACE's reimplementation of SERAC-style routing: a scope classifier plus a small linear counterfactual model.

name: GRACE
note: Lifelong editing with a discrete key-value codebook that replaces one layer's activation when a key is within its radius.

name: Unedited model
note: The base model before any edit (reported as 'w/o Editing' or 'Pre-edited').

name: Generative Agents
note: Park et al. (2023): memory stream retrieved by a weighted sum of min-max-normalised recency, importance and relevance.

name: All memories in context
note: Generic baseline: every stored memory is put in the context with no retrieval (EMG-RAG's NiaH, THEANINE's 'All Memories').

name: M-RAG
note: RAG over multiple database partitions with multi-agent RL (ACL 2024): Agent-S picks a partition, Agent-R refines memories.

name: Keqing
note: Knowledge-graph QA that splits a question into sub-questions, retrieves candidate entities, answers each and merges the answers.

name: Direct inference
note: The LLM answers the question directly, with no retrieval, tools or memory; search-agent baseline as in Search-R1.

name: SFT (search-agent baseline)
note: Supervised fine-tuning on question-answer data without search, as the SFT baseline in Search-R1's QA tables.

name: R1 (RL without search)
note: DeepSeek-R1-style RL on the QA training data, reasoning and answering without a search engine; variant names base or instruct start.

name: Rejection sampling
note: Fine-tuning on the model's own sampled trajectories that reached the correct answer, with search; Search-R1 QA baseline.

name: Contriever
note: Unsupervised dense bi-encoder retriever trained with contrastive learning; used as a plain passage retriever baseline.

name: GTR
note: Generalizable T5-based dense bi-encoder retriever; plain passage retriever baseline.

name: ColBERTv2
note: Late-interaction (token-level MaxSim) passage retriever; plain passage retriever baseline.

name: Proposition (Dense X)
note: Passages rewritten by an LLM into atomic propositions that are indexed and retrieved instead of passages; variant names the retriever.

name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill (generic reasoner)
note: DeepSeek-R1-distilled Llama/Qwen models used as a generic long-CoT reasoning baseline without user history.

name: OPPU
note: One PEFT Per User (Tan et al., 2024): per-user LoRA personalization, trained on other users' history first.

name: KV-Mem
note: Key-value memory networks (Miller et al., 2016); KGQA baseline.

name: EmbedKGQA
note: KG-embedding-based multi-hop KGQA (Saxena et al., ACL 2020).

name: NSM
note: Neural State Machine KGQA with teacher-student intermediate supervision (He et al., WSDM 2021).

name: TransferNet
note: Transparent multi-hop KGQA over relation graphs (Shi et al., EMNLP 2021).

name: KGT5
note: Sequence-to-sequence KG completion and QA (Saxena et al., ACL 2022).

name: GraftNet
note: Early fusion of KB and text with graph propagation (Sun et al., EMNLP 2018).

name: PullNet
note: Iterative question-specific subgraph retrieval with GCNs (Sun et al., EMNLP 2019).

name: SR (Subgraph Retriever)
note: Trainable subgraph retriever decoupled from the reasoner (Zhang et al., ACL 2022); reported as SR+NSM.

name: KD-CoT
note: Knowledge-driven chain-of-thought verified against a KG (Wang et al., arXiv preprint).

name: UniKGQA
note: Unified retrieval and reasoning for multi-hop KGQA (Jiang et al., ICLR 2023).

name: KG-CoT
note: Chain-of-thought over KGs with a small graph reasoning model (Zhao et al., IJCAI 2024).

name: SubgraphRAG
note: Lightweight MLP with parallel triple scoring for subgraph retrieval, then an LLM reasons (Li et al., ICLR 2025).

name: AWM (Agent Workflow Memory)
note: Induces reusable workflows from past trajectories and adds them to the agent's memory (as described in Skill-Pro §5.1).

name: MindAct
note: Mind2Web's baseline agent: element ranker top-50 then LLM multi-choice action selection.

name: RCI
note: Recursively Criticizes and Improves: LLM plan + self-correction on MiniWoB++ (Kim et al., NeurIPS 2023).

name: AdaPlanner
note: Adaptive planning from environment feedback (Sun et al., 2023).

name: Pix2Act
note: Pixel-based agent trained with BC and tree search (Shaw et al., 2023).

name: CC-Net
note: BC + RL on 2.4M MiniWoB++ demonstrations (Humphreys et al., ICML 2022).

name: WebGUM
note: Multimodal fine-tuned web agent (Furuta et al., 2023).

name: WebN-T5
note: T5 fine-tuned on 12k MiniWoB++ demonstrations (Gur et al., 2023).

name: Prior MiniWoB++ methods (aggregate)
note: 'Others' column of Synapse Table 3: aggregated baselines before CC-Net (Shi et al. 2017; Liu et al. 2018; Gur et al. 2018; Jia et al. 2018).

name: Memory Retrieval (MSC)
note: Retrieval of the k most similar summarized memory sentences for response generation (Xu et al., 2022, Beyond Goldfish Memory); k=6 in THEANINE.

name: COMEDY
note: Compress to Impress: LLM summarizes sessions and compresses them into events, user portrait and user-bot relation for response generation.

name: In-context learning (many-shot)
note: Task demonstrations from the training split placed in the prompt, all of them or as many as fit the context window (ACE §4.2).

name: GEPA
note: Reflective prompt optimiser: collects execution traces, reflects in natural language and evolves prompts with a genetic Pareto search; run via DSPy with auto="heavy" in ACE.

name: MIPROv2
note: DSPy prompt optimiser that jointly tunes instructions and few-shot demonstrations by Bayesian optimisation.

name: Dynamic Cheatsheet (DC)
note: Test-time memory of reusable strategies and code snippets that an LLM rewrites after each input; ACE runs the cumulative mode (DC-CU).

name: LightRAG
note: Graph-based RAG with LLM-extracted entities and relations and dual-level (entity and relation) retrieval combined with chunks.

name: PathRAG
note: Graph RAG on the same entity-relation graph as LightRAG that retrieves relational paths and prunes them (as summarised in HyperGraphRAG Table 1 and App. F).

name: Stella (stella_en_1.5B_v5)
note: Dense text embedding model distilled from larger embedders (Jasper and Stella).

name: BGE-M3
note: Multilingual, multi-granularity dense embedding model (Chen et al., 2024).

name: LongMemEval RAG pipeline
note: Retrieval-augmented memory design from the LongMemEval paper, as used by Associa: Stella retriever with user facts concatenated to keys (UF), optional LLM time filtering (TF), and Chain-of-Note reading in JSON format.

name: Buy and hold
note: Passive trading baseline: buy the stock at the start of the test period and keep it.

name: FinGPT
note: Open-source financial LLM framework (Yang et al., 2023) used as an LLM trading-agent baseline.

name: A2C (DRL trading agent)
note: Advantage actor-critic deep-RL trading agent on numeric market features (Stable-Baselines3).

name: PPO (DRL trading agent)
note: Proximal policy optimization deep-RL trading agent on numeric market features (Stable-Baselines3).

name: DQN (DRL trading agent)
note: Deep Q-network trading agent on numeric market features (Stable-Baselines3).

name: Router-KNN
note: LLM router that assigns a query to the LLM favoured by its nearest neighbours in embedding space (Shnitzer et al., 2023).

name: Router-MLP
note: MLP router over query embeddings (Shnitzer et al., 2023).

name: Router-SVM
note: SVM router over query features, from RouterBench (Hu et al., 2024).

name: RouterDC
note: Query-based LLM router trained with dual contrastive learning (Chen et al., NeurIPS 2024).

name: GraphRouter
note: Single-round LLM router posed as edge prediction on a query-task-LLM graph (Feng et al., 2024).

name: Prompt LLM (router)
note: Baseline from Router-R1: an LLM prompted to pick LLMs over several rounds, no routing module.

name: Router-KNN-MR
note: Multi-round extension of Router-KNN, from Router-R1.

name: R2-Reasoner
note: Route-and-Reason: a reinforced model router that decomposes a task and routes sub-tasks (Shao et al., 2025).

name: Router-R1
note: LLM router trained with RL to interleave thinking and routing over several rounds (Zhang, Feng, You, 2025).

name: ALBERT
note: 'A lite BERT' encoder; fine-tuned PLM baseline for temporal KGQA (MemoTime ref [21]).

name: CronKGQA
note: Embedding-based temporal KGQA that aligns question embeddings with time-stamped triples (Saxena et al., ACL 2021; MemoTime ref [36]).

name: MultiQA
note: Embedding-based multi-granularity temporal KGQA from the MultiTQ paper (Chen et al., ACL 2023; MemoTime ref [5]).

name: ChatGPT (GPT-3.5-Turbo)
note: GPT-3.5-Turbo prompted directly, as reported in temporal KGQA papers.

name: KG-RAG (temporal KGQA baseline)
note: LLM in-context baseline combining a temporal KG with GPT-3.5-Turbo, as reported in the ARI paper (MemoTime ref [4]).

name: ReAct KB
note: ReAct-style agent over a temporal KG with GPT-3.5-Turbo, as reported in the ARI paper (MemoTime ref [4]).

name: ARI
note: Abstract reasoning induction for temporal KGQA with GPT-3.5-Turbo (Chen et al., ACL 2024; MemoTime ref [4]).

name: TempAgent
note: Time-aware ReAct agent for temporal KGQA with GPT-3.5-Turbo (Hu et al., Findings of NAACL 2025; MemoTime ref [13]).

name: UNIQORN
note: Unified QA over RDF knowledge graphs and text (Pramanik et al., Journal of Web Semantics 2024; MemoTime ref [34]).

name: TempoQR
note: Temporal question reasoning over KGs with embeddings (Mavromatis et al., AAAI 2022; MemoTime ref [28]).

name: EXAQT
note: Complex temporal QA on KGs; the paper that introduced TimeQuestions (Jia et al., CIKM 2021; MemoTime ref [18]).

name: TwiRGCN
note: Temporally weighted graph convolution for temporal KGQA (Sharma et al.; MemoTime ref [38]).

name: LGQA
note: Local and global information fusion for temporal QA (Liu et al., IJCAI 2023; MemoTime ref [25]).

name: GenTKGQA
note: Two-stage generative temporal KGQA that fine-tunes LLaMA2-7B (Gao et al., ACL 2024; MemoTime ref [11]).

name: TimeR4
note: Time-aware RAG for temporal KGQA: a jointly fine-tuned retriever feeding ChatGPT (Qian et al., EMNLP 2024; MemoTime ref [35]).

name: Random history items
note: Personalization baseline that puts k randomly chosen documents from the user's history into the prompt.

name: Most recent history items
note: Personalization baseline that puts the user's k most recent documents into the prompt.

name: ROPG
note: Retrieval optimization for personalized generation (Salemi et al., SIGIR 2024): retriever trained from feedback on LLM generations.

name: CFRAG
note: RAG with collaborative filtering for personalized text generation (Shi et al., SIGIR 2025): also retrieves from similar users' histories.

name: Memory-R1
note: LLM agents trained with reinforcement learning to manage and use an external memory (arXiv 2508.19828).

name: SPARQA
note: Skeleton-based semantic parsing for complex KBQA (Sun et al., AAAI 2020); listed as 'SPARQL' in RoG Table 1.

name: QGG
note: Query graph generation for multi-hop complex KBQA (Lan & Jiang, ACL 2020).

name: ArcaneQA
note: Dynamic program induction and contextualized encoding for KBQA (Gu & Su, COLING 2022).

name: RnG-KBQA
note: Generation-augmented iterative ranking of logical forms for KBQA (Ye et al., ACL 2022).

name: DECAF
note: Joint decoding of answers and logical forms for KBQA (Yu et al., ICLR 2023); RoG reports the DPR+FiD-3B variant.

name: Oracle messages
note: Reference, not a system: the gold evidence messages are given to the answer model, so only generation is tested.

name: Self-Consistency (CoT-SC)
note: Sample several chain-of-thought answers and take the majority (Wang et al., ICLR 2023); no external knowledge.

name: Prior fine-tuned SOTA
note: Placeholder for the best previously published fine-tuned result on each dataset as cited by Think-on-Graph Table 1; a different system per dataset (named in the row variant).

name: KB-BINDER
note: Few-shot in-context KBQA: Codex drafts logical forms that are bound to the KB (Li et al., ACL 2023).

name: CBR-KBQA
note: Case-based reasoning for KBQA: retrieves similar solved questions and adapts their logical forms (Das et al., 2021).

name: TIARA
note: Multi-grained retrieval of KB items to guide logical-form generation (Shu et al., EMNLP 2022).

name: StructGPT
note: Prompting framework in which the LLM reads structured data through interface calls (Jiang et al., 2023).

name: STM
note: Space-Time Memory network for video object segmentation: every memory frame is kept and read by attention (Oh et al., ICCV 2019).

name: STCN
note: Space-time correspondence network with L2 similarity and shared keys (Cheng et al., NeurIPS 2021); XMem's working-memory baseline.

name: AOT
note: Associating Objects with Transformers for VOS (Yang et al., NeurIPS 2021); XMem compares the R50 variant.

name: CFBI
note: Collaborative foreground-background integration VOS (Yang et al., ECCV 2020); temporally local memory.

name: CFBI+
note: Multi-scale CFBI (Yang et al., TPAMI 2021).

name: RMNet
note: Efficient regional memory network for VOS (Xie et al., CVPR 2021).

name: HMMN
note: Hierarchical memory matching network for VOS (Seong et al., ICCV 2021).

name: MiVOS
note: Modular interactive VOS with propagation and fusion modules (Cheng et al., CVPR 2021); evaluated with BL30K pretraining.

name: JOINT
note: Joint inductive and transductive learning for VOS with a local memory window (Mao et al., ICCV 2021).

name: AFB-URR
note: Adaptive feature bank that merges similar features and evicts least-used ones, for long videos (Liang et al., NeurIPS 2020).

name: GEAR
note: Graph-based evidence aggregating and reasoning for fact verification (Zhou et al., 2019); SimGRAG uses its KG version trained on FactKG.

name: KELP
note: KG-enhanced LLMs via a trained path-selection model (Liu et al., 2024); 1- or 2-hop paths from oracle entities.

name: G-Retriever
note: Retrieves similar nodes and relations, builds a prize-collecting Steiner tree subgraph and encodes it with a GNN for a frozen LLM (He et al., 2024).

name: KAPING
note: Knowledge-augmented LM prompting: retrieves KG triples by embedding similarity to the question and prompts zero-shot (Baek et al., NLRSE workshop 2023).

name: KG-GPT
note: Segments the query and lets an LLM pick matching KG relations per segment, starting from given entities (Kim et al., 2023).

name: CAD (context-aware decoding)
note: Contrastive decoding that amplifies the difference between output distributions with and without the retrieved context (Shi et al., NAACL 2024).

name: AdaCAD
note: Context-aware decoding whose contrast weight adapts to the measured conflict between context and parametric knowledge (Han et al., NAACL 2025).

name: Adaptive-RAG
note: A trained classifier predicts question complexity and chooses the retrieval strategy (Jeong et al., NAACL 2024); CARE uses a binary retrieve / no-retrieve variant.

name: SKR-kNN
note: Self-knowledge guided retrieval: kNN over embeddings of training questions the LLM got right or wrong without retrieval decides whether to retrieve (Wang et al., EMNLP 2023).

name: Priori Judgment
note: The LLM is prompted to say whether it can answer (with the passage shown); 'unknown' falls back to the closed-book answer (Ren et al., COLING 2025).

name: RetRobust
note: Fine-tunes the LLM with irrelevant and distracting retrieved contexts so it learns to ignore them (Yoran et al., ICLR 2024).

name: Direct FT (conflict-aware fine-tuning of the LLM)
note: Baseline built in the CARE paper: CARE's positive / hard-negative training applied to the base LLM with LoRA instead of a context assessor.

name: Instruct model, prompted
note: The instruction-tuned base model used zero-shot as the agent, with no training on the environment ('Prompt' rows in Early Experience).

name: Imitation learning (SFT on expert trajectories)
note: Behaviour cloning: next-token SFT of the same base model on expert (state, action) pairs; the IL baseline in Early Experience, with the same step budget.

name: STaR-style rationales
note: Zelikman et al. (2022): fine-tune on model-written rationales for the expert action, without looking at alternative actions or their outcomes.

name: DPO
note: Direct Preference Optimization (Rafailov et al., 2023); in Early Experience the expert action is 'chosen' and a rolled-out non-expert action 'rejected'.

name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
note: Proprietary LLM prompted as an agent; Early Experience copies its ALFWorld and WebShop numbers from Feng et al. (2025).

name: GPT-4-Turbo
note: Proprietary LLM prompted as a web agent; Early Experience copies its WebArena-Lite number from Qi et al. (2025).

name: Reset (train from scratch)
note: Continual-RL baseline: re-initialise the network at every new task (DQN-Reset / SAC 'independent' in FAME); reference for forward transfer.

name: Finetune
note: Continual-RL baseline: keep training the same network from task to task with no protection against forgetting.

name: Average (TD-target averaging)
note: FAME's Meta-World baseline: the critic's TD target is averaged over the agents of all past tasks.

name: DQN MultiHead
note: DQN with one output head per task, given the task identity (baseline from Anand & Precup, 2023).

name: DQN LargeBuffer
note: DQN with a larger replay buffer that keeps past-task data (500k transitions in FAME's code).

name: PT-DQN
note: Permanent + transient value functions (Anand & Precup, NeurIPS 2023): a slow permanent network plus a fast transient one per task.

name: PackNet
note: Mallya & Lazebnik (CVPR 2018): prunes and freezes a subset of weights per task; zero forgetting, needs task identity.

name: Progressive Networks
note: Rusu et al. (2016): adds a new column per task with lateral connections to frozen earlier columns.

name: CompoNet
note: Self-composing policies (Malagon et al., ICML 2024): a growing set of policy modules combined by attention.

name: RMT (Recurrent Memory Transformer)
note: Segment-level recurrence through memory tokens written by a forward pass; two-segment version in GradMem.

name: ARMT (Associative Recurrent Memory Transformer)
note: RMT with per-layer associative memory matrices updated DeltaNet-style.

name: Mamba / Mamba-2
note: Selective state-space sequence model; its recurrent state acts as memory. GradMem uses Mamba-2 (130M) and a 4-layer version.

name: Pythia
note: Pretrained decoder LM suite; Pythia-160m fine-tuned with full context as an upper bound in GradMem.

name: UI-TARS
note: Native GUI agent model (7B and 72B rows in SE-GA). SE-GA cites the UI-TARS-2 technical report (arXiv 2509.02544) for it.

name: Qwen2.5-VL
note: Open vision-language model; 7B and 72B rows; SE-GA's base model.

name: Aria-UI
note: GUI grounding model (23B per SE-GA Table 1).

name: SeeClick
note: GUI grounding agent (9.6B); also introduced ScreenSpot.

name: UGround
note: GUI grounding baseline (7B). SE-GA cites arXiv 2510.03853 for it and also lists Gou et al., arXiv 2410.05243 ('universal visual grounding for GUI agents') in its references.

name: OS-Atlas
note: Foundation action model for GUI agents (7B).

name: Aguvis
note: Pure-vision GUI agent (7B).

name: OS-Genesis
note: GUI agent trained on reverse-synthesised trajectories (7B).

name: GUI-Critic-R1
note: Pre-operative error-diagnosis critic for GUI automation (7B row on AndroidWorld).

name: Claude 3 Opus (as named by SE-GA)
note: SE-GA §5.2 names the baseline Claude3-Opus but cites Anthropic's 2024 'Our 3.5 models and computer use' post; the tables just say Claude.

name: Video-LLaVA
note: Open video LVLM (7B); baseline host model in Video-RAG Table 1.

name: Long-LLaVA (aws-prototyping/long-llava-qwen2-7b)
note: The Hugging Face model cited as [45] in Video-RAG, not the LongLLaVA hybrid-architecture paper (arXiv 2409.02889).

name: VITA-1.5
note: Open omni-modal LVLM; row in Video-RAG Table 1.

name: Video-XL
note: Long-video LVLM; row in Video-RAG Table 2 (MLVU).

name: Aria
note: Open multimodal mixture-of-experts model; row in Video-RAG Tables 2-3.

name: Oryx MLLM
note: Row in Video-RAG Table 2 (MLVU).

name: PLLaVA
note: Row in Video-RAG Table 3 (LongVideoBench).

name: ShareGPT4Video
note: Row in Video-RAG Table 3 (LongVideoBench).

name: LLaVA-NeXT (Mistral-7B)
note: Image LVLM; row in Video-RAG Table 3.

name: VideoChat2 (Mistral-7B)
note: Row in Video-RAG Table 3; the paper gives no reference for it (only VideoChat, arXiv 2305.06355, is cited).

name: Orca
note: LLM serving system with iteration-level scheduling (OSDI 2022). Not public; vLLM compares against its own reimplementation in three reservation variants (Max, Pow2, Oracle).
